title: Sew on a button
intro: Lost a button? Sew it back on in ten minutes, with a shank so it fastens properly.

steps.t: Cut about [[60 cm]] of thread, pass it through the needle, bring the two ends together and knot them.
Find the spot from the old thread holes or by closing the buttonhole over the fabric, and mark it with chalk.
steps.q: Does the mark line up with the buttonhole and the other buttons?
steps.fix: Close the garment as if buttoned and push a pin straight through the middle of the buttonhole: that's the spot.

steps.t: Come up from the back right on the mark and make a tiny stitch to anchor the thread.
Place the button on the mark and lay a pin across the top, between the holes: it's your spacer.
Sew from hole to hole over the pin 4-6 times. With 4 holes, make two parallel lines or a cross, like the others.
Pull out the pin, lift the button and wind the thread 5-6 times round the stitches underneath: that's the shank.
Push the needle to the back, make 2-3 tiny stitches in the same spot, knot and cut the thread.
Do it up: the button should slip through the buttonhole without pulling the fabric.
steps.q: Does the button fasten without pulling the fabric?
steps.fix: If it pulls, redo it with a thicker spacer, like a toothpick. If it wobbles, add a few more passes.

tips: For coats, use stronger thread and a matchstick as the spacer: you get a longer shank.
Button with a loop underneath: no spacer needed, just sew 6-8 times through the loop and finish off.
Run the thread over a wax candle: it tangles less and holds better.

title: Hand-sew a hem
intro: Trousers or skirt too long? Hem them by hand with a blind stitch that barely shows outside.

steps.t: Put the garment on with the shoes you'll wear, fold the hem inside to the right length and pin it at the front.
Take it off, lay it flat and pin the fold all the way round. Copy the same measurement onto the other leg.
Measure both legs from the crotch seam to the fold, or a skirt from the waist at several points: they must match.
steps.q: Are both legs the same length?
steps.fix: Move the pins on the longer leg until the measurements match, then try the garment on again.

steps.t: Press the fold with the iron: the crease is your guide for the whole job.
Open the fold and draw a chalk line [[3-4 cm]] below the pressed crease.
Cut off the extra fabric along the line with sharp scissors.
Turn the cut edge under by [[1 cm]], fold the hem back up on the crease and pin it.
Thread a single strand of about [[60 cm]], knot it and hide the knot inside the fold.
Blind stitch: pick up 1-2 threads of the outer fabric, then slide the needle [[1 cm]] inside the fold. Repeat.
Check the right side: the stitches should be tiny and the fabric shouldn't pucker.
steps.q: Do the stitches barely show on the right side, with the fabric flat?
steps.fix: Pick up fewer threads on the outside and don't pull the thread tight: keep it relaxed.

steps.t: At the end, make 2-3 tiny stitches inside the fold, knot and cut the thread.
Press the hem from the inside. On dark fabric, put a damp cloth in between so it doesn't go shiny.

tips: Use thread a shade darker than the fabric: it hides better on the right side than a lighter one.
Not sure about the length? Don't cut: hem it with all the fabric folded inside.
Jeans and very thick fabrics are better done by machine or by a tailor: by hand it's hard work.
